answer.rationale: Write-path p99 began climbing shortly after a release shipped 2 hours ago, during peak settlement writes. The strongest temporal signal is the release, and memory_b1 records that a rollback cleared a similar checkout error spike without customer impact. Rollback is reversible, removes the suspected cause, and preserves in-flight customer writes better than failover or capacity changes, which don't address a likely code regression. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing target dependency/read load, not write-path latency. Verifying b1 (rollback precedent) and b3 (capacity, the main alternative) before committing.
